sowhat.text: A 10-year at 5.05% and an 85% chance of a December hike raise financing costs, yet stock-for-stock energy deals and a BDC merger still got done. Brent at $115 keeps energy dealmaking active.

pitch: Stocks edged up again Wednesday. The S&P gained about 0.3 percent to 7,744. The Fed held at 3.75 to 4 percent, but two officials voted for a hike, and markets now see about an 85 percent chance of a December hike. The 10-year rose to 5.05 percent. Oil rose after an attack on a Saudi refinery, with Brent at about 115 dollars. On M&A, EQT is buying Range Resources in an all-stock deal over 50 billion dollars, Ares Capital agreed to buy MidCap Financial for about 2.6 billion, and HealthSpan is buying Surgery Partners for about 5.7 billion. Credit is open but selective.

quiz.a: Wells Fargo, which also provided $750M of secured financing.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $115.32 and WTI at $102.78 on Wednesday, up after an attack on a Saudi refinery. The WTI–Brent spread is about $13. High prices support producer cash flow and funding for energy M&A like EQT-Range.

EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal, pro forma EV over $50B, with Citi and RBC advising EQT and Evercore and J.P. Morgan advising Range. Ares Capital is buying MidCap Financial for about $2.6B EV, advised by Wells Fargo. HealthSpan is buying Surgery Partners for about $5.7B EV.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: Thursday's GDP and core PCE, since the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% and markets see about an 85% chance of a December hike. Then Amazon earnings for AI capex, and Exxon and Chevron on Friday for the energy read.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The discount rate rises, so present value falls, and terminal value falls most because it is the longest-dated cash flow. With the 10-year already at 5.05%, another 50 bp would pressure long-duration equity values and make leveraged buyouts harder to finance.
chat.tip: State direction, then the terminal value point.

chat.q: Why would EQT pay in stock for Range?
chat.a: An all-stock deal avoids new borrowing when the 10-year is 5.05% and a December hike is priced at about 85%. Range holders get about 27% of the combined company and share in about $325M of base synergies expected within two years. The tradeoff is dilution and two shareholder votes.

chat.q: How would you describe credit markets today?
chat.a: Open but selective. The latest FRED reading, from 27 Oct, showed high yield at 318 bp and investment grade at 88 bp, tight by history. Octus reported weaker deals pulled, such as AVI-SPL's $690M loan, while Crescent Energy's $1.5B term loan priced.
chat.tip: Give both sides: tight spreads, picky buyers.
